_doc: Tess OS Keystone manifest — hand-authored per spec kb/wiki/synthesis/2026-06-27-keystone-architecture.md §2.4. THIS IS THE UPDATER'S WRITE-SCOPE GUARD. Do NOT auto-glob: this repo mixes framework content with clients/, kb/, example-project/, .venv/ and stray root files. tessctl may write ONLY to paths matching owned_globs (refined per-file by tess.lock status). Everything else is unreachable. never_touch is an explicit belt-and-suspenders denylist for user data, secrets, and known-stray junk; precedence: owned_globs WINS over never_touch (so clients/_template/** stays framework-owned even though clients/*/** is denied).

render_targets._doc: Phase 1 (HIGH-1 / MED-3, Fable review) — PER-INSTALL render-target enablement. `tessctl render` with no flags, and `tessctl update`'s Step 7, render only the targets named in `enabled` — NOT every target registered in the RENDER_TARGETS registry (.tess/bin/tessctl). This is what stops a Claude-only install from silently starting to emit e.g. codex/AGENTS.md the moment a Phase 2+ target is added to the registry: a target must be registered AND enabled here to be rendered by default. `tessctl render --target <name>` explicitly bypasses this list (an operator naming a target by hand is not the silent-default case this guards). Missing this key entirely (a manifest that predates Phase 1) defaults to the same effective value: ["claude-code"]. Phase 2 (Codex + generic targets) registers both in RENDER_TARGETS but deliberately does NOT add them here yet — adapters/README.md's own rollout note: the future harness-select wizard axis (axis 6) is meant to write this list PER-INSTALL based on what the operator actually uses, not have the engine hardcode one global default that force-renders AGENTS.md/.codex/** onto every Claude-Code-only install. Preview/adopt explicitly today via `tessctl render --target codex` / `--target generic`, or add the name here yourself.

_owned_notes.CLAUDE.md: entry-point doctrine; rendered from CLAUDE.md.tpl + operator/ stubs on update (status core-managed, tier security for its rule blocks).
_owned_notes.conductor/**: the doctrine files; guardrails.md / verification-routing.md / channel-guardrails.md / dispatch-brief.md carry tier:security in tess.lock.
_owned_notes.agents/**: 165 persona prose specs (the agents/ subtree). Framework-owned per spec §2.1 CORE territory and the §2.4 manifest example. NOTE: this was NOT in the caller's parenthetical owned list; added because these are core content, not user data — omitting them would orphan every persona spec from updates. User-authored agents live at .claude/agents/<custom>.md and are protected per-file via tess.lock status:user-created, NOT by excluding this glob.
_owned_notes..claude/agents/**: the 42 compiled dispatch definitions. Per-file status in tess.lock governs actual write behavior: core-managed agents merge; status:user-created agents are never read, never touched.
_owned_notes..claude/commands/**: 26 slash-command definitions (defect #9): core source at .tess/core/commands/**; live at .claude/commands/**. Workflows decision: .claude/workflows/ (3 files — daily-error-report.js, mission-execution.js, clienta-incident.js) are instance-specific operator automation, NOT framework content — they remain user-space and are excluded from core/owned_globs.
_owned_notes..claude/hooks/**: the 6 guard hooks. LOW-2 (Fable review): the render pipeline supports a {{TESS_ROOT}} template token (apply_token_sub in .tess/bin/tessctl), but none of the 6 shipped hooks carry it — they resolve their project root at RUN time via the $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR env var Claude Code injects, not at RENDER time. LF-enforced (CRLF breaks the shebang).
_owned_notes..claude/settings.json: rendered every update from settings-core.json (spec Decision 8). LOW-2 (Fable review): settings-core.json also uses $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, not the {{TESS_ROOT}} token — zero core files ship the literal token today. This is WHY rendered output is byte-identical regardless of machine/root: no absolute path is ever baked into the file at render time; {{TESS_ROOT}} substitution exists in the engine (tested directly in tests/test_render.py) for a future core file that needs it, it just isn't exercised by anything currently shipped. Customize via `tessctl publish --tag settings`.
_owned_notes.clients/_template/**: client-folder scaffold — framework-owned (spec §2.4). Distinct from real clients under clients/*/** which are never_touch.
_owned_notes.core/contracts/**: Phase 0/1/2/Goal-5 contracts-as-code: brief/crew-plan/verdict/return-manifest/policy/mission/retry JSON schemas + README, the machine-checkable half of the doctrine (spec: docs/ULTIMATE_FRAMEWORK_PLAN.md Phase 0 Decision #3 + Phase 1 item 1, 'wire the deferred Phase-0 contracts into the managed set' + Phase 2 item 4, 'policy.schema.json... build it now' + Goal #5 §C3/§C4, mission.schema.json/retry.schema.json). Core source at .tess/core/contracts/**; live at core/contracts/** — same pristine-mirror pattern as conductor/**. brief.schema.json + verdict.schema.json + policy.schema.json carry tier:security in tess.lock (they encode conductor/dispatch-brief.md, conductor/verification-routing.md, and conductor/guardrails.md Rule 18, all already tier:security); mission.schema.json/retry.schema.json are tier:normal (their doctrine sources, doctrine.md/subagent-failure-protocol.md, are not themselves tier:security).
_owned_notes.core/policy/**: Phase 2 (`tessctl gate` spine, Design Decision #2/#6): the policy-AS-DATA instance (core/policy/policy.yaml) the gate reads to classify changed paths and decide what needs a covering APPROVE verdict — the machine-readable half of conductor/verification-routing.md + conductor/guardrails.md Rule 18. tier:security in tess.lock for the same reason as the two schemas above: silently weakening this file (e.g. deleting a rule that used to gate a real prod path) is exactly as consequential as editing the doctrine prose. Core source at .tess/core/policy/**; live at core/policy/** — same pristine-mirror pattern as conductor/**.
_owned_notes.AGENTS.md: Phase 2 (Codex + generic render targets): the portable doctrine digest — render_agents_md() in .tess/bin/tessctl, composed from .tess/core/templates/agents-md/AGENTS.md.tpl + 4 REUSED claude-md/ fragments (rule-zero.md, hard-floor.md, system-laws.md, directory.md) + harness-note.md + a generated command table. Owned jointly by the `codex` and `generic` targets (byte-identical output either way — see render_agents_md()'s docstring); NOT tess.lock-tracked as a per-file entry the way CLAUDE.md is (its render_generated status is instead asserted via the render-target registry, same as every RenderTarget-compiled artifact).
_owned_notes..codex/prompts/**: Phase 2 (`codex` render target): 1:1 mirrors of `.tess/core/commands/*.md` into Codex CLI's native custom-prompt convention. Render-generated by CodexRenderTarget.render() (its own copy-phase — NOT `tessctl restore`, which is Claude-Code-shaped); drift-checked by doctor/verify via the untracked-render-generated pass (`_check_untracked_render_generated`) rather than individual tess.lock entries, since the underlying `.tess/core/commands/*.md` source is already base_sha-pinned by the pre-existing `.claude/commands/**` lock entries.
_owned_notes..codex/config.toml: Phase 2 (`codex` render target): project-scoped approval_policy/sandbox_mode defaults, rendered from .tess/core/templates/agents-md/codex-config.toml.tpl. Codex only loads this for a project marked trusted by the operator.
_owned_notes.prompts/**: Phase 2 (`generic` render target): plain, tool-agnostic mirrors of `.tess/core/commands/*.md` for any AGENTS.md-reading agent with no harness-specific prompt convention of its own. Same render-generated / untracked-drift-check treatment as `.codex/prompts/**` above.

_never_touch_notes.kb/**: internal + client knowledge base (raw/wiki/lint); Tess-maintained user space.
_never_touch_notes.clients/*/**: real client operating systems — data, secrets, repos. clients/_template/** is the sole exception (owned_globs wins).
_never_touch_notes.operator/**: user-authored identity & context, injected at CLAUDE.md render time.
_never_touch_notes..env / .env.* / .claude/settings.local.j: secrets and local allowlists; Claude Code merges settings.local.json natively.
_never_touch_notes.*.local.md / **/*.local.md: append-first shadow files — the 80% customization path (spec §5 Layer 2); appended after core on resolve, never overwritten.
_never_touch_notes..tess/*: tessctl's own transactional state (snapshots, staging, provenance log, lock). NOTE: .tess/core/** is the pristine merge-base source — read by tessctl, never a live-tree write target, so it is intentionally absent from BOTH lists.
_never_touch_notes..tess/trace/**: Goal #8: the no-mission-id fallback trace-log path (.tess/trace/runs/<run_id>.jsonl) — local runtime state written directly by `_trace_append_event` (never through guarded_write / the manifest write-gate), same bucket as .tess/snapshots/** and .tess/staging/** above. Mission-scoped trace events (missions/<id>/trace.jsonl) are NOT covered by this entry — they are mission-record data, the same un-manifested bucket missions/<id>/verdicts/** already lives in.
_never_touch_notes.python/data layer: main.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .python-version, .venv/** — the repo's Python/uv tooling, not framework doctrine.
_never_touch_notes.example-project/ , starter/ , docs/ , in: non-framework subtrees present in this messy repo; explicitly fenced off.
_never_touch_notes.adapters/**: Phase 1 render-target-adapter documentation seam (docs/ULTIMATE_FRAMEWORK_PLAN.md Part B architecture; item 3 of the Phase 1 brief). Pure prose describing the RenderTarget interface implemented in .tess/bin/tessctl (RENDER_TARGETS registry) — same fenced-off treatment as docs/**, since there is no core->live split to track here (no .tess/core/adapters/** mirror exists; nothing to render). Phase 2 (Codex + generic targets) confirms this still holds: their rendered config fragment (.codex/config.toml) sources from .tess/core/templates/agents-md/codex-config.toml.tpl, NOT from anything under adapters/ — adapters/codex/README.md and adapters/generic/README.md (like adapters/claude-code/README.md before them) are hand-authored docs, not compiled artifacts. Revisit only if a future target ever needs to render something FROM adapters/**.
_never_touch_notes.missions/**: Goal #5 (tessctl mission + the typed-retry ledger) — PER-PROJECT mission records `tessctl mission new`/`gate clear`/`retry log` write at runtime (mission.md/mission.json, retries/<task>.attempt-N.md). User/mission DATA, not framework doctrine — same fenced-off treatment as kb/**/clients/*/**, and (like adapters/**/docs/**) there is no .tess/core/missions/** mirror; nothing here is rendered from core. missions/README.md (the convention doc) is a hand-authored, plain committed file, same as adapters/*/README.md.
_never_touch_notes..tess/state/**: Phase 0.1 (cross-harness shared brain, docs/STATE_LAYER.md) — the canonical harness-neutral runtime-state root: memory/, tasks/, ledger/, locks/. Both Claude Code and Codex mount THIS tree for shared state (the architecture principle: shared state lives in harness-neutral files both harnesses mount, never in a harness's private home dir). Same bucket as missions/**/kb/**: PER-INSTANCE DATA, not framework content — there is no .tess/core/state/** mirror, nothing here is rendered from core, and `tessctl restore`/`render`/`update` never touch it. Ships EMPTY in the public scaffold (only .gitkeep placeholders under each subdir) — adopters inherit the structure, never any instance's actual memory/task/ledger data (same scaffold-strip precedent create-tess's ignore.js already applies to .tess/snapshots/.tess/staging). Phase 0.1 ships the fenced store only; the memory-adopt symlink, tasks CLI, and ledger read/write commands are Phase 0.2+.
